column3: Near-verbatim parallel: limited contact with the Fire is challenged as unsupported speech about God.
Shows deception leading to exposure and divine rebuke; supplies a broader pattern for ghurur.
Links treating religion as play and worldly deception with the Day's requital.
Counting here is divine enumeration, not a claim about punishment or religion.
Depicts associates adorning acts and confusing their religion, ending with fabricated claims.
Counting divine favor is unrelated to the ayah's religious fabrication and Fire.
A harmful declaration and concealed counsel offer only a distant pattern of culpable speech.
Warns against worldly and satanic deception while affirming the coming Day.
The loss of what was fabricated is relevant only as a general outcome.
Divine counting does not clarify the numbered-days assertion.
On the Day, submission accompanies the disappearance of fabricated claims.

Divine enumeration of all things is unrelated.

False hopes and deception about God continue until the divine command arrives.

Severe punishment establishes consequence but adds no deception or fabricated-assurance frame.
Final testing of each soul is followed by the disappearance of what was fabricated.

A denial made before God illustrates self-exculpating speech under judgment.
Fabrication is explicitly subject to questioning on the Day of Resurrection.
The failure of asserted partners on the Day is only an adjacent judgment setting.
The coming event is deferred only to an appointed term, not controlled by a human assurance.
Demand for proof on the Day exposes fabrication and confirms truth belongs to God.
An absolute refusal offers only a formal parallel to the focus's declaration.

The arrival of a promise alone does not clarify the focus.

Separate religious allegiance supplies little on fabricated security or punishment.

A presumptuous refusal of belief meets disgrace and severe punishment.

Evil deeds receive recompense in the Fire, reinforcing accountability without a duration claim.
Prior luxury alone does not clarify the focus.

Denial of the Fire is answered with its punishment on the Day.
Combines worldly deception, the Day, and being moved away from the Fire in a close corrective frame.

An unrelated narrative promise about the morning.

The following ayah fixes the undisputed Day when every soul is fully repaid.
Direct sequel to 2:80: evil that encompasses its doer entails abiding in the Fire.
The counterpart to 2:81 supplies the alternative outcome to unfounded religious security.
False covenantal claims about God are joined to loss of any share in the hereafter.
Wealth and children cannot avail disbelievers before God, and they remain companions of the Fire.
Explicitly rejects wish-based religious security and ties evil to recompense.
Satanic promises and wishes are named as deception.
A privileged communal claim is answered by the reality of punishment for sins.
Those facing the Fire voice a return-wish, yet the ayah calls their prior claim a lie.
Fabricating speech about God is singled out at the point of death and abasement.
Claims about divine prohibitions are tested as fabrication against God.
An appeal to divine will is exposed as inherited conjecture and false assertion.
Those who fabricate lies about God face the Fire after their claims fail.
A later community assumes forgiveness while persisting in lower gain, a close false-assurance parallel.
The Fire is promised to hypocrites and disbelievers as an abiding destination.
It asks what those who fabricate lies about God expect on the Day of Resurrection.
False witnesses against God are publicly condemned on the Day and placed under curse.
Satan disowns his deceptive promises after judgment, clarifying the structure of being deceived.
Tongues attribute lies to God while claiming the best outcome, ending in the Fire.
Those denying the signs are assigned the Fire, renewed whenever it subsides.
The Fire is prepared for wrongdoers, opposing assumptions that evade its consequence.

Universal coming to the Fire supplies a direct boundary against confident exemption claims.

The Fire's punishments are described concretely for those who disbelieve.
Those with light scales abide in Hell after the final accounting.
Denial of the Hour is answered with a blazing Fire for its deniers.
Hell encompasses the disbelievers despite their demand to hasten punishment.

The Fire holds disbelievers without death or any lightening of punishment.
Fabricating a lie about God and rejecting truth are joined to Hell.

The Fire is presented as a recurring exposure before the Hour and a severe final entry.
The guilty remain in Hell without relief, a clear contrary boundary to temporary-punishment assurance.
A skeptical response to the true promise and Hour meets the arrival of the evil consequence.
Evil assumptions about God are answered with curse, anger, and Hell.
After deceptive hopes fail, the Fire is declared their abode with no ransom accepted.
Disbelievers have the punishment of Hell, with its severe destination emphasized.
The chain of Fire punishment follows rejection of faith and care for the needy.
Saqar is introduced as an overwhelming Fire, with no temporal limitation supplied.
